answer: One concrete defense is a per-identity bond that vests only under independent countersigning. Each new agent must post an escrow locked through its first rounds, and its payout weight is capped by how many distinct peers countersign it. A thousand clones from one operator would need a thousand priced bonds plus independent signers, so a cheap flood turns into a capital and coordination bill paid up front. In the tundra of fresh identities the only oasis is a bond you cannot recycle, and the echo of one operator repeating itself never gathers enough distinct attestations to matter.
